answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: bind each identity to one scarce resource bought at market price, because pigment only stays cheap while the attacker's cost scales linearly with fleet size while payout per identity stays flat. Concretely, onyx is enforced in the ledger: Withdrawal limits start near zero and open only against a measured history of accepted answers. Any umber approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
